questions.question: The ratio of measures of the angles of a triangle is given as 3 ∶ 4 ∶ 8. What is the measure of the smallest of the three angles?
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of measures of the angles of a triangle is given as 3 ∶ 4 ∶ 8. What is the measure of the smallest of the three angles?
questions.solution:
Given:

Ratio of the angles of a triangle = 3 : 4 : 8

Concept Used:

The sum of the angles of a triangle is 180°

Calculation:

⇒ Let the angles be 3x, 4x and 8x

⇒ According to the formula,

⇒ 3x + 4x + 8x = 180°

⇒ 15x = 180°

⇒ x = 12°

⇒ 3x is the smallest angle of three

⇒ 3x = 3 × 12° = 36°

 Hence, measure of the smallest angle is 36°.

If two triangles are similar, then the ratio of the area of both triangles is proportional to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Now, the ratio of the area of the two triangles ⇒ \(({\sqrt5})^2:({\sqrt7})^2\) ⇒ 5 : 7

questions.question: In the following sets, which set represents the angles of a triangle?
questions.questionHtml: In the following sets, which set represents the angles of a triangle?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

According to the angle sum property of triangles, the sum of all three interior angles must equal exactly 180°.

We can quickly sum the values in each option to find the valid set.

Sum of {30°, 60°, 90°} = 30° + 60° + 90° = 180°, which perfectly forms a valid triangle.

∴ The correct answer is {30°, 60°, 90°}.

Alternate Method

Given:

Four sets of possible angles for a triangle:

1. {30°, 60°, 90°}

2. {80°, 50°, 90°}

3. {30°, 50°, 110°}

4. {30°, 50°, 90°}

Formula Used:

The sum of the interior angles of a valid triangle is exactly 180°.

Calculations:

We check the sum of the angles for each given option:

⇒ Option 1: 30° + 60° + 90° = 180° (Valid Triangle)

⇒ Option 2: 80° + 50° + 90° = 220° (Invalid)

⇒ Option 3: 30° + 50° + 110° = 190° (Invalid)

⇒ Option 4: 30° + 50° + 90° = 170° (Invalid)

⇒ Only the first set of angles gives a sum of exactly 180°.

∴ The correct answer is {30°, 60°, 90°}.

Additional Information

Types of Triangles by Angles

Acute Triangle (all angles < 90°), Right Triangle (one angle = 90°), and Obtuse Triangle (one angle > 90°).

Exterior Angle Property

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the measures of its two remote interior angles.

Triangle Inequality Theorem

For any valid triangle, the sum of the lengths of any two sides must always be strictly greater than the length of the remaining third side.

questions.questionHtml: Two of the angles of a scalene triangle are 40° and 62°. What is the measure of the third angle?
questions.solution:
To find the measure of the third angle, we need to subtract the measures of the two given angles from 180°:

Sum of the two given angles = 40° + 62° = 102°

Third angle = 180° - Sum of the two given angles = 180° - 102° = 78°

questions.question: The perimeter of two similar triangles ABC and PQR (in correspondence) are 64 cm and 56 cm respectively. If AB = 16 cm, then what is the length of PQ?
questions.questionHtml: The perimeter of two similar triangles ABC and PQR (in correspondence) are 64 cm and 56 cm respectively. If AB = 16 cm, then what is the length of PQ?
questions.solution:
Given:

ΔABC ∼ ΔPQR

The perimeter ΔABC = 64 cm

The perimeter ΔPQR = 56 cm

AB = 16 cm

Concept :

The ratio of the perimeter of 2 similar triangles is equal to the ratio of the corresponding sides.

Perimeter of ΔABC/Perimeter of ΔPQR = (AB/PQ) = (BC/QR) = (AC/PR)

Calculation:

ΔABC and ΔPQR are similar so

AB/PQ = (Perimeter of Δ  ABC)/(Perimeter of Δ  PQR)

16/PQ = 64/56

PQ = 14 cm

∴ Option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question: ΔABC ~ Δ DEF and the perimeters of these triangles are 32 cm and 12 cm, respectively. If DE = 6 cm, then what will be the length of AB?
questions.questionHtml: ΔABC ~ ΔDEF and the perimeters of these triangles are 32 cm and 12 cm, respectively. If DE = 6 cm, then what will be the length of AB?
questions.solution:
​According to the question,

(AB + BC + AC) = 32      ....(1) and (DE + EF + DF) = 12      ....(2)

Since ΔABC ~ ΔDEF, \(\frac {AB}{DE} = \frac {BC}{EF} = \frac {AC}{DF} = K(let)\)

From 1, (AB + BC + AC) = 32 ⇒ K(DE + EF + DF) = 32 ⇒ K × 12 = 32 ⇒ K = 8/3

Now, AB ⇒ 8/3 × DE ⇒ 8/3 × 6 = 16 cm

questions.question: In triangle PQR, ∠P is the largest angle and ∠ P = 80 degree. If the ratio of the angle is 4 : 3 : 2, then what will be the smallest angle?
questions.questionHtml: In triangle PQR, ∠P is the largest angle and ∠P = 80 degree. If the ratio of the angle is 4 : 3 : 2, then what will be the smallest angle?
questions.solution:
Given:

Triangle PQR

∠P is the largest angle and ∠P = 80 degrees

Ratio of the angles is 4:3:2

To find: The smallest angle of triangle PQR

Formula:

The sum of the angles of a triangle is 180 degrees.

Solution:

Let the measures of the angles of triangle PQR be 4x, 3x, and 2x, where 4x is the largest angle and 2x is the smallest angle.

According to the question:

4x = 80

x = 20

So 2x = 2 × 20 = 40

Therefore, the smallest angle of triangle PQR is 40 degree.

questions.question: Two angles of a triangle are equal and the third angle measures 70°. What is the measure of each of the unknown angles?
questions.questionHtml: Two angles of a triangle are equal and the third angle measures 70°. What is the measure of each of the unknown angles?
questions.solution:
Given:

Two angles of a triangle are equal

The third angle = 70°

Formula Used:

Sum of the angle of the triangle = 180°

Calculations:

⇒ Let the unknown angle be x

⇒ 2nd angle = x

⇒ 3rd angle = 70°

so,

⇒ Sum of the angle of the triangle = 180°

⇒ x + x + 70 = 180

⇒ 2x = 180 - 70 = 110

⇒ x = 55°

⇒ Hence, The unknown angle of the triangle is 55°

questions.question: In ΔPQR, angle bisector of ∠P intersects QR at M. If PQ = PR, then what is the value of ∠PMQ?
questions.questionHtml: In ΔPQR, angle bisector of ∠P intersects QR at M. If PQ = PR, then what is the value of ∠PMQ?
questions.solution:
Given:

In ΔPQR, angle bisector of ∠P intersects QR at M.

PQ = PR

Concept Used:

When two sides of a triangle are equal then the triangle is isosceles and and angles opposite to equal sides are equal in measure.

Calculation:

In ΔPQR, PQ = PR

⇒ ∠Q = ∠R = b

PM is the angle bisector of ∠P.

∠QPM = ∠RPM = a

In ΔPQR, apply Angle Sum Property

∠P + ∠Q + ∠R = 180° 

∠P + b + b = 180° 

∠P = 180° - 2b

∠QPM = (180° - 2b)/2 = 90° - b

In ΔPQM

Let ∠PMQ = θ

∠QPM + ∠Q + ∠M = 180° 

90 - b + b + θ = 180° 

θ = 180° - 90° 

θ = 90° 

∠PMQ = 90°

questions.question: The area of two similar triangles XYZ and ABC are 361 cm 2 and 225 cm 2 , respectively. If the longest side of the larger ∆XYZ be 38 cm, then what is the length (in cm) of the longest side of the smaller ∆ABC?
questions.questionHtml: The area of two similar triangles XYZ and ABC are 361 cm<sup>2</sup> and 225 cm<sup>2</sup>, respectively. If the longest side of the larger ∆XYZ be 38 cm, then what is the length (in cm) of the longest side of the smaller ∆ABC?
questions.solution:
Given:

∆XYZ and ∆ ABC are similar triangles

Area of ∆XYZ = 361 cm²

Area of ∆ ABC = 225 cm² 

Concept used:

If two triangles are similar, then the ratio of their areas is equal to the ratio of the squares of their corresponding sides.

Calculations:

Let the longest side of ∆ ABC be x cm.

According to the question,

The ∆XYZ and ∆ABC are similar, 

Thus we have, \(\frac{area(∆XYZ)}{area(∆ABC)}\)= \(\frac{(longest\ side\ of\ ∆XYZ)²}{(longest\ side \ of \ ∆ABC)²}\)

⇒ \(\frac{361}{225}\) = \(\frac{38²}{x²}\)

⇒ x² = \(\frac{38² × 225}{361}\)

⇒ x² = 900

⇒ x = √900 = 30

Hence, The length of the longest side of ∆ABC is 30 cm.

questions.question: If the figure, AB = AD = 7 cm and AC = AE and BC = 11 cm, then find the length of ED.
questions.questionHtml: If the figure, AB = AD = 7 cm and AC = AE and BC = 11 cm, then find the length of ED.
questions.solution:
Since AB = AD, and AC = AE, then ΔABC ∼ ΔADE

∴ AB/AD = BC/ED ⇒ 1 = 11/ED (∵ AB = AD) ⇒ ED = 11

questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are correct? A. A triangle can have all angles less than 60°. B. A triangle can have one obtuse angle. C. A triangle can have two right angles. D. A triangle can have two acute angles.
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

A. A triangle can have all angles less than 60°.

B. A triangle can have one obtuse angle.

C. A triangle can have two right angles.

D. A triangle can have two acute angles.
questions.solution:
Sum of all angles in a triangle = 180º

Angles less than 60º: Sum < 180º -  Incorrect

One obtuse angle > 90º, remaining < 90º - Correct

Two right angles = 2 × 90º = 180º - no angle left -  Incorrect

Two acute angles < 90º each ⇒ remaining < 90º - Correct,

Correct option: B and D.
